facts.statement: The genus Goronyosaurus was established by Azzaroli and colleagues in 1972.
facts.quote: parent_authority: Azzaroli et al., 1972

facts.statement: The species Goronyosaurus nigeriensis was originally described by Swinton and others in 1930.
facts.quote: authority: (Swinton et al., 1930)

facts.statement: The type specimen was initially named Mosasaurus nigeriensis in 1930 before being moved to its own genus.
facts.quote: The type specimen was first described in 1930 as Mosasaurus nigeriensis

facts.statement: Unique anatomical adaptations found in later fossils led to the reclassification of the species into the new genus Goronyosaurus in 1972.
facts.quote: subsequent remains revealed a highly unique set of adaptations that prompted the species to be reclassified as the only species of the new genus Goronyosaurus in 1972

facts.statement: Fossils of Goronyosaurus are exclusively known from the Late Maastrichtian period in West Africa.
facts.quote: Fossils of Goronyosaurus are exclusively known from the Late Maastrichtian of the Iullemmeden Basin in West Africa

facts.statement: Fossils have been found in the Dukamaje Formation of Niger and Nigeria and the Farin Doutchi Formation of Niger.
facts.quote: specifically the Dukamaje Formation of Niger and Nigeria and Farin Doutchi Formation of Niger

facts.statement: Goronyosaurus possesses teeth that are unlike those of any other mosasaur.
facts.quote: Goronyosaurus possesses unique teeth, which are unlike the teeth of any other mosasaur

facts.statement: The original type specimen, consisting of two vertebrae, was noted by Franz von Nopcsa in 1925 in northwestern Nigeria.
facts.quote: The type specimen of Goronyosaurus, BMNH R 5674 consisting of two vertebrae, was found within a section of the Dukamaje Formation called the "Mosasaurus shales" in northwestern Nigeria and was noted by Franz von Nopcsa in 1925

facts.statement: The remains were described more completely by Swinton and colleagues in 1930.
facts.quote: these remains were described more completely by Swinton et al. in 1930

facts.statement: Additional material cataloged as IGF 14750 was recovered between 1969 and 1971 by two Italian expeditions sponsored by the National Research Council and the National Lincean Academy.
facts.quote: Later from 1969-1971, two Italian expeditions into same locality sponsored by the National Research Council and National Lincean Academy respectively recovered additional material cataloged as IGF 14750

facts.statement: Azzaroli and colleagues named the new genus Goronyosaurus based on differences found in the Nigerian fossils.
facts.quote: Azzaroli et al. named a new genus Goronyosaurus

facts.statement: The generic name Goronyosaurus honors the Goronyo District of Nigeria where the fossils were discovered.
facts.quote: The generic name recognizes the Goronyo District of Nigeria, where the material was found

facts.statement: Because the original type specimen's status was unknown, the authors designated IGF 14750 as the replacement neotype.
facts.quote: With no knowledge on the whereabouts or status of BMNH R 5674, the authors designated IGF 14750 as the taxon's replacement neotype

facts.statement: A second, unnamed species from the Farin Doutchi Formation in Niger was reported by Lingham-Soliar in 1991.
facts.quote: A second, unnamed species, from the Farin Doutchi Formation in Niger was reported on by Lingham-Soliar (1991)

facts.statement: Goronyosaurus is a small mosasaur that measured up to 5.14 meters in length.
facts.quote: Goronyosaurus is a small mosasaur, measuring up to 5.14 m long

facts.statement: Soliar derived a body length estimate of 5.14 meters from a skull length of 0.71 meters.
facts.quote: Soliar (1988) derived a body length estimate of 5.14 m from a 0.71 m long skull

facts.statement: The premaxillae bear strong teeth, with the frontmost tooth positioned directly behind the start of the snout.
facts.quote: The premaxilae bear strong teeth, with the anterior most tooth being placed directly behind the beginning of the snout

facts.statement: The maxillae bones are unusual for mosasaurids because they bear teeth that extend behind the front of the eye socket.
facts.quote: The maxillae bones are unusual for mosasaurids, as they bear teeth which extend posterior to the front of the orbit

facts.statement: There are probably around eleven teeth in the maxilla, though the exact number is uncertain due to breakage.
facts.quote: there is probably around eleven

facts.statement: The nasal openings in Goronyosaurus are relatively small and positioned towards the back of the skull.
facts.quote: The nasal openings themselves are relatively small and posterior in Goronyosaurus

facts.statement: Azzaroli and colleagues proposed in 1972 that Goronyosaurus had an extremely long and tall jugal bone, a view later disputed.
facts.quote: Azzaroli et al. (1972) proposed that Goronyosaurus has an extremely long and tall jugal, which directly contrasts with the thin slender bones of other lepidosaurs

facts.statement: Soliar disregarded Azzaroli's functional implications for the jugal bone in 1988 due to a lack of precedent for such an adaptation.
facts.quote: The functional implications proposed by Azzaroli were disregarded by Soliar in 1988, due to there being no precedent for such a mechanical adaptation

facts.statement: Halstead and Middleton doubted the identity of the jugal bones in 1982, leading Soliar to propose in 1988 that the structure was a taphonomic mix of the jugal and mandible.
facts.quote: The identity of the jugals was doubted by Halstead & Middleton (1982), and Soliar (1988) instead proposed that the "jugal" of Azzaroli et al. was instead a taphonomic combination of the jugal and coronoid process of the mandible

facts.statement: The true jugal bone is estimated to be around 19 mm thick across most of its structure, similar to Liodon.
facts.quote: The true jugal would be only around 19 mm thick across a majority of its structure, similar in anatomy to Liodon

facts.statement: The strongly built parietal bones are very narrow and broken.
facts.quote: The strongly built parietals are very narrow, and are broken

facts.statement: The prefrontal bones are crushed and distorted but were likely positioned like those of Tylosaurus in life.
facts.quote: The prefrontals are very crushed and distorted out of their original articulation, but were positioned like Tylosaurus in life

facts.statement: Multiple dorsal vertebrae are known, with centra that begin cylindrical but become flattened near the pelvis.
facts.quote: Multiple dorsal vertebrae are known from along the back. Their centra begin as cylindrical, but become flattened closer to the pelvis

facts.statement: Zygapophyses are weakly present in dorsal vertebrae, unlike in the cervical vertebrae, but inter-arch articulations are absent in both.
facts.quote: Zygapophyses are weakly present, unlike in the cervical vertebrae, but the inter-arch articulations are still absent

facts.statement: Goronyosaurus was originally classified in its own subfamily, Goronyosaurinae, but this classification was later found to be incorrect.
facts.quote: Goronyosaurus was originally named within its own subfamily, Goronyosaurinae.

facts.statement: In 1988, Lingham-Soliar placed Goronyosaurus within the subfamily Tylosaurinae based on cranial characteristics.
facts.quote: Lingham-Soliar found that Goronyosaurus was within Tylosaurinae in 1988, based on a phylogeny of cranial-only characters.

facts.statement: A 2010 analysis suggested Goronyosaurus belongs in Mosasaurinae because it forms a clade with Prognathodon, Plesiotylosaurus, and Ectenosaurus.
facts.quote: A placement within the Tylosaurinae is not necessarily correct however, as the genus was found as forming a clade with the genera Prognathodon, Plesiotylosaurus and Ectenosaurus, which would place it within the Mosasaurinae, in a comprehensive 2010 analysis of the Anguimorpha.

facts.statement: Strong et al. assigned Goronyosaurus to the subfamily Plioplatecarpinae in 2020.
facts.quote: In 2020, Strong et al. assigned Goronyosarus to the Plioplatecarpinae in a clade containing Angolasaurus and Selmasaurus.

facts.statement: William Swinton described the species as Mosasaurus nigeriensis in 1930 based on jaw fossils from Maastrichtian deposits.
facts.quote: Fue descrito en 1930 por William Swinton como «Mosasaurus» nigeriensis basándose en algunos fósiles de mandíbulas en depósitos del Maastrichtiense.

facts.statement: A group of Italian researchers elevated the species to its own genus in 1972 based on new findings.
facts.quote: Fue considerado como un género aparte en 1972 por un grupo de investigadores italianos, sobre la base de nuevos hallazgos.

facts.statement: Goronyosaurus reached a length of about seven meters with a skull measuring 62 centimeters.
facts.quote: Goronyosaurus medía unos siete metros de largo, con un cráneo que alcanzaba los 62 centímetros de longitud.

facts.statement: The skull and teeth resemble crocodiles, featuring ten elongated canine-like teeth that interlocked with holes in the opposite jaw.
facts.quote: El cráneo y los dientes tiene cierta similitud con el de los cocodrilos y poseen diez dientes caniniformes alargados, los cuales se encajaban en unas aberturas o agujeros en la mandíbula opuesta.

facts.statement: Goronyosaurus had relatively longer jaws than other mosasaurs, with jaw muscles positioned further back to allow for a rapid bite.
facts.quote: Sus quijadas eran relativamente más largas que las de otros mosasáuridos, con los músculos mandibulares situados más hacia atrás para permitir una rápida mordida.

facts.statement: Goronyosaurus had small eyes and relied more on touch and smell, as suggested by nerve traces in its snout.
facts.quote: Sus ojos eran pequeños, dependiendo más de sus sentidos del tacto y del olfato, como sugiere los trazos de los nervios en el hocico.

facts.statement: Studies indicate Goronyosaurus teeth were better adapted for cutting meat than piercing bones.
facts.quote: Un estudio de sus dientes indica que estaban mejor adaptados para cortar carne que para atravesar huesos.

facts.statement: Goronyosaurus likely inhabited turbid waters like estuaries and fed on large fish and other marine reptiles.
facts.quote: Probablemente residía en hábitats con aguas turbias, tales como los estuarios y se alimentaba de grandes peces y otros reptiles marinos.

facts.statement: Unlike most mosasaurs with cutting teeth, Goronyosaurus had straight teeth with rounded apices designed for smashing food.
facts.quote: Unlike a majority of mosasaurs, which have cutting teeth, Goronyosaurus has straight teeth with a rounded apex designed more for smashing food.

facts.statement: All known Goronyosaurus fossils come from the Dukamaje and Farin Doutchi Formations in Niger and Nigeria, located within the Iullemmeden Basin.
facts.quote: All known Goronyosaurus fossils come from the Dukamaje and Farin Doutchi Formations of Niger and Nigeria, both of which lie within the Iullemmeden Basin.

facts.statement: Goronyosaurus specialized in a crocodile-like skull with an elongated rigid build and interlocking teeth, suited for hunting in murky settings.
facts.quote: The specialization towards a crocodile-like skull through an elongated and rigid tube-like build, straight conical interlocking teeth, and highly developed snout sensitivity and sense of smell was well-suited for pursuing prey in the environment's unique murky setting.

facts.statement: Lingham-Soliar (1999) suggested Goronyosaurus represented an early stage of adaptation to freshwater rivers, a transition that was likely prevented by the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction.
facts.quote: Lingham-Soliar (1999) opined that Goronyosaurus represented an incipient stage towards a freshwater invasion of rivers, which would have been achieved had it not been for the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction.

facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)
